name: Question 11
problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt{x+2}$ and the $y$-axis from $y=2$ to $y=3.$ Which integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
worked_solution:
The volume of the solid generated when the region bounded by a curve $x=g(y),$ the $y$-axis, and the horizontal lines $y=c$ and $y=d$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
V=\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}[g(y)]^{2}\text{d}y.
$$

First, we write our equation in terms of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{x+2} \\ {y}^{2} & =x+2 \\ x & ={y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our example, $g(y)={y}^{2}-2$ and the limits of integration are from $y=2$ to $y=3.$

Finally, the volume can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}{[g(y)]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}{({y}^{2}-2)}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}({y}^{4}-4{y}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve y=x+2 and the y-axis from y=2 to y=3. Which integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis?

a
∫23(y4−4y2+4)dy
b
∫23(y2−2)dy
c
π∫23(y+2)dy
d
π∫23(y4−4y2+4)dy
e
π∫23(y2−2)dy
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The volume of the solid generated when the region bounded by a curve x=g(y), the y-axis, and the horizontal lines y=c and y=d is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis is given by V=π∫cd[g(y)]2dy.

First, we write our equation in terms of y:

y=x+2y2=x+2x=y2−2

So, in our example, g(y)=y2−2 and the limits of integration are from y=2 to y=3.

Finally, the volume can be found as follows:

V=π∫cd[g(y)]2dy=π∫23(y2−2)2dy=π∫23(y4−4y2+4)dy
